reserveReview.reviewer: PoR verification sweep 2026-08 (lockstep coherent refresh: report and composition review updated together from the same artefact)
reserveReview.rationale: Deloitte's June 30, 2026 examination (opinion dated 2026-07-29, PDF read this pass) reports EURC reserves of EUR 384,737,359 against 381,986,779 EURC in circulation, composed entirely of cash held at regulated financial institutions (EUR 389,833,314 less EUR 5,095,955 of net settlement timing). No securities are held. The report does not split deposits between systemically important and other institutions, so the prior two-way split is merged into one examined cash category.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Deloitte examination of the EURC Reserve Report as of June 30, 2026
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: No material unclassified reserve exposure is present in Circle's two-category disclosure; individual deposit institutions are not named.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Circle's ACPR-filed MiCA white paper (section D.3) states that funds received in exchange for EURC are protected against any recourse by other creditors of Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, including in enforcement or insolvency proceedings, and the EURC Terms and Deloitte's May 2026 examination define reserves as unencumbered segregated accounts apart from corporate funds, held on behalf of and for the benefit of holders. Bank identities, institution count, provider-level shares, custodian-replacement arrangements, and rehypothecation terms are not published; the May 2026 report shows the reserve is 100% cash at regulated financial institutions. Issuer pages describe the reserve banks as regulated financial institutions in the EEA, while one circle.com/eurc footnote states cash is held at US financial institutions; account-level placement is not public.
